sections.h2: Which selling paths suit a Horizon City owner?
sections.html:
Use a broker, sell privately, or take cash. Census data shows owners in 85.2% of Horizon City homes, so most sellers are families giving up a house they have lived in.

Lean toward cash when you need a firm closing day or hate the idea of paying for repairs. Pick a listing if the house is in good order and a buyer's loan timeline does not bother you. Whichever you pick, do the same prep first.

  • Gather your deed, the newest tax statement and any utility district bills.
  • Ask each buyer for terms in writing: price, closing day and who pays what.
  • Ask for proof of funds before you stop showing the house.

sections.h2: Where is Horizon City and how was it built?
sections.html:
The town's comprehensive plan places Horizon City on the Hueco Bolson about 15 miles east of El Paso, with the Franklin Mountains to the west and Mexico roughly 20 miles south. The plan gives 4,022 feet of elevation, about 7.77 inches of annual rain, and a July average high of 94 degrees Fahrenheit.

According to that plan, a Chicago-based developer announced the project in December 1959, and a planning outfit from Tucson laid the town out beside the proposed Interstate 10 route. The first house sold on October 31, 1962, and by 1971 only about 94 homes were occupied. Horizon City incorporated on August 13, 1988, and voters adopted a charter in November 1997. It is a home rule city with a mayor and seven council members.

Desert sun and dry air are tough on roofs, stucco and paint, and inspectors check cooling equipment closely. Handle cheap repairs before showing the house, or price in the ones you leave.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Horizon City homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts the midpoint home value at $170,200 for 2020 to 2024, and the 2025 head count of 25,118 sits 11.8% over the 2020 base of 22,461. Steady growth keeps new subdivisions coming, so your house competes with new construction.

Households average 3.39 people, so buyers often want extra bedrooms. The 29.4-minute average commute points to workers heading into El Paso, which makes access to Interstate 10 and Eastlake Boulevard part of what you are selling.

sections.h2: Who is buying in Horizon City, and what do they want?
sections.html:
Horizon City skews young. Children make up 33.7% of residents and seniors just 5.5%, per QuickFacts, and 92.5% of people kept the same address for a year, which points to settled families. Larger households tend to look for extra bedrooms, a yard and an easy run to Interstate 10.

Language plays a part as well. 73.5% of residents speak something other than English at home, and 23.2% were born abroad. If a family member who reads Spanish will help you with the sale, ask the buyer to give you the contract and disclosures in a form you can read before you sign.

Median household income is $65,737, and the poverty rate is 22.0%. A clean, working house with a documented repair history will draw more interest than one with open questions.

sections.h2: Does the town have rules for building and land use?
sections.html:
Yes. Per the comprehensive plan, a Planning and Zoning Commission and a Board of Adjustment advise the council on zoning and other development matters. If you added a room, fence, carport or pool, ask town hall whether it was permitted, because lenders and title companies sometimes ask.

The plan also notes that the town has about 5.7 square miles within its limits as of 2011, while QuickFacts counts 8.71 square miles of land in 2020, so ask the town for the current boundary. If your lot is near the edge, confirm whether it sits inside the town or in the county, since that decides who issues permits and provides services.

The same plan suggests studying bike routes, sidewalks and street lighting on principal streets such as Darrington Road and Eastlake Boulevard. Buyers who care about traffic and walkability may ask about plans for the street your house faces.

sections.h2: Which schools and offices matter to a Horizon City seller?
sections.html:
The plan names the Socorro and Clint school districts and the Horizon Regional Municipal Utility District among local agencies. Buyers ask which district serves a home, so confirm it on your tax bill.

El Paso County's Central Appraisal District appraises every parcel of real property and business personal property inside the county. Its home page links to protests and appeals, exemption forms, a deadline calendar and a taxpayer liaison who helps with complaints about the review board. Check that calendar for the protest date that applies to you.

  • Appraisal district: your value and exemptions.
  • County tax office: the bill and a payoff statement.
  • County clerk: deed and other recorded papers.
  • Town hall: permits, zoning and utility accounts.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded in El Paso County and what does it cost?
sections.html:
The El Paso County Clerk records deeds. A land deed is accepted for filing only after the signer acknowledges it before a notary or comparable officer, or two witnesses swear to it.

In the 2023 clerk manual from Texas Courts, page one costs $5.00, every added page $4.00, and each indexed name past five adds $0.25. It also lists records fees, such as $2.00 for technology and up to $10 each for management and archive. A missing grantee address can add $25. Fees change, so check the clerk's current schedule.

A title company normally files the deed for you. Filing happens in the county containing the land, which for a Horizon City house is El Paso County. The manual mentions no transfer tax. A settlement statement from your title company will itemize every charge on your side.

sections.h2: What does an unpaid tax bill mean for a sale?
sections.html:
Each year's tax lien fastens to the land on January 1 and stays with the land through a sale. The Comptroller adds that a court can order the property sold even after a transfer, which is why clear title waits on delinquent taxes.

A bill left open past January 31 is late, and charges start accruing February 1. Should the house be auctioned for taxes, an opinion of the Texas Supreme Court explains the buy-back right. Homestead, farm and mineral land gets two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed, at a 25 percent markup in the first year and 50 percent in the second. Other land gets 180 days. Any surplus from a tax sale can be claimed by the former owner for two years, according to the State Law Library.

If you are behind, selling before a suit saves court costs. Get a payoff figure from the tax office, and ask about an installment plan, which some collectors grant on a residence homestead.

faqs.q: How many people live in Horizon City?
faqs.a: About 25,118, per the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate, an 11.8% gain on the 2020 base.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax when I sell?
faqs.a: The county clerk manual lists recording fees and says nothing of a transfer tax. Ask your title company for the full settlement statement.

faqs.q: Can I sell with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the balance is cleared by closing, because the lien stays with the house. The county tax office can issue a payoff statement.

faqs.q: Who decides the value of my property for tax?
faqs.a: The El Paso Central Appraisal District. Use its calendar for protest dates and its taxpayer liaison if you have a complaint.

faqs.q: Is $170,200 the price my house will fetch?
faqs.a: It is a townwide midpoint from the 2020 to 2024 survey. Ask for written offers or an appraisal for your own address.
